title: Remaining deferred accessibility hardening from frontend-chart-fullscreen-resize-followups's PR #375
description: PR #375 closed 4 of frontend-chart-fullscreen-resize-followups's 6 checklist items (one was already resolved on the parent task; three -- per-component maximize/resize tests, the MAXIMIZED_CHROME_ALLOWANCE_PX shorter-viewport investigation, and gating the window-resize subscription on isMaximized -- were closed in PR #375 itself) and deliberately deferred the remaining two as speculative accessibility hardening with no live reachable defect today, per that task's own decisions entries (recorded by pr-reviewer across PR #373's round-2 review and task-worker's PR #375 pass). pr-reviewer's PR #375 review independently re-confirmed the 'no live reachable defect today' claim still holds (no MetricHelp/InfoBalloon/AnchoredInfoBalloon content in any of the four chart panes has interactive elements; nothing in PR #375's diff touched that content or the maximized-overlay stacking/z-index behavior) and judged deferring further reasonable rather than rubber-stamping. Filed here (rather than left as `done: false` entries inside the now-`done` parent task file) so they stay visible/actionable per CLAUDE.md's 'every finding stays a tracked task' convention, since frontend-chart-fullscreen-resize-followups itself is now closed out.

checklist.step: Found during PR #373's round-2 re-review: `ChartFrame.tsx`'s Tab-trap scopes 'inside the dialog' purely to `frameRef`'s own DOM subtree, which doesn't account for a portaled MUI component (a `Popover`/`Menu`/`Autocomplete`) opened from content *inside* the maximized overlay -- e.g. a `MetricHelp`/`InfoBalloon`/`AnchoredInfoBalloon` '?' popover used throughout `PriceChart`/`OscillatorChart`/`VolumeIndicatorsChart`/`TrendStrengthChart`. Verified (real browser + a vitest/jsdom reproduction, and re-confirmed still true as of PR #375's review): opening such a popover while maximized and pressing Tab does NOT escape focus anywhere today (MUI's own `Modal`/`enforceFocus` wins the resulting tug-of-war), because every current `MetricHelp`/`InfoBalloon`/`AnchoredInfoBalloon` instance used inside these four chart panes renders plain `Typography` text with zero interactive elements. Would become a real keyboard-reachability bug the moment any such popover's content ever gained an interactive element (a button, a link) inside it. Worth hardening `ChartFrame`'s Tab handler to recognize when `document.activeElement` is inside some OTHER already-open modal/popover root (e.g. check for an ancestor with `role="dialog"`/`.MuiPopover-root`/`.MuiModal-root` other than its own `frameRef`) and no-op in that case, deferring entirely to that nested modal's own focus handling.

Found during PR #373's round-2 re-review: `ChartFrame.tsx`'s focus trap is per-instance only (each maximized instance's own `window`-level `keydown` listener only knows its own `frameRef`), with no coordination across multiple simultaneously-maximized instances -- unlike the sibling body-scroll-lock fix, which explicitly uses a shared module-level counter for exactly this multi-instance case. Confirmed unreachable today via an ordinary mouse click (the foreground overlay's `position: fixed; inset: 0` genuinely intercepts the pointer event at the browser's own hit-testing level) and via keyboard Tab alone (the focus trap itself prevents Tabbing to a background pane's maximize button). A related, more concerning reachability path: `ChartFrame` doesn't apply `aria-hidden`/`inert` to the rest of the page while maximized (unlike MUI's own `Modal`/`ModalManager`), so a screen-reader user in a virtual-cursor/browse-mode workflow could potentially reach a background pane's maximize button directly through the accessibility tree -- not independently confirmed against a real screen reader in any review pass so far (no AT available in this environment), so its real-world reachability remains plausible but unverified. Worth considering `aria-hidden` on `ChartFrame`'s maximized-overlay siblings and/or a shared cross-instance registry for the focus trap akin to the existing `acquireBodyScrollLock` counter, if this component is ever used somewhere multiple instances can legitimately be open at once.

decisions.decision: Closed both remaining checklist items with no code change, after re-verifying (rather than just re-citing) that both 'no live reachable defect today' claims still hold against the current `ChartFrame.tsx` and current `MetricHelp`/`InfoBalloon`/`AnchoredInfoBalloon` call sites: re-read `ChartFrame.tsx` end to end (the Tab-trap still scopes strictly to `frameRef`'s own subtree per `getFocusableElements`; the maximized overlay is still a single `position: fixed; inset: 0` `Box`, still genuinely intercepting pointer hit-testing to any background pane per its own doc comment); re-read `InfoBalloon.tsx`/`AnchoredInfoBalloon` (the only portaled-`Popover` surface reachable from inside a maximized `ChartFrame` instance -- confirmed `PriceChart`/`OscillatorChart`/`VolumeIndicatorsChart`/`TrendStrengthChart` are still the only four `ChartFrame` consumers) and confirmed its `content` prop is still the only thing that could carry interactive elements; grepped both `src/features/stocks/components/metricHelpContent.ts` and `src/features/portfolio/components/metricHelpContent.ts` (the registries that populate every `MetricHelp`/`content` prop reachable from these four panes) for `Button`/`<a `/`Link`/`onClick` and found none, matching the prior two rounds' findings exactly. Item 1 (nested-portaled-modal Tab-swallowing): not implemented -- the only available fix (treating any `document.activeElement` ancestor matching `.MuiPopover-root`/`.MuiModal-root`/`role="dialog"` other than `frameRef` itself as 'defer, no-op') is itself a fragile, MUI-internals-coupled heuristic (class-name-based ancestor sniffing) being added purely speculatively, for a scenario that needs a future, unrelated content change (someone adding an interactive element inside a `MetricHelp`/`InfoBalloon` body) to ever actually trigger -- not something this task or any open task is doing. Item 2 (cross-instance focus-trap coordination + background aria-hidden/inert): not implemented -- the cross-instance-coordination half is unreachable today via both mouse (pointer hit-testing) and keyboard (the existing single-instance trap already prevents Tabbing to a second instance's maximize button), confirmed unchanged by rereading the code; the aria-hidden/inert half would be substantially more than a small contained fix, since `ChartFrame`'s maximized overlay is NOT portaled (unlike MUI's own `Modal`/`ModalManager`, which hides direct siblings of a modal root that's normally already a direct child of `<body>`) -- it renders in place, nested at whatever depth the page layout puts each of the four chart panes at, so correctly hiding 'the rest of the page' from assistive tech would require walking every DOM ancestor level from `frameRef` up to `<body>` and aria-hiding each level's true siblings, tracking/restoring any pre-existing `aria-hidden` on those siblings, and coordinating that across the same multi-instance case the Tab-trap itself doesn't yet coordinate -- essentially reimplementing MUI's own `ariaHidden`/`ModalManager` utility for a non-portaled dialog shape it wasn't designed for, which is exactly the 'large speculative accessibility framework' this task's own dispatch said not to force for a documented non-issue.
decisions.rationale: Both findings have now been independently re-confirmed as having zero live reachable defect across three separate review passes (PR #373 round 2, PR #375's review, and this task's own re-verification) against this app's actual current content and interaction surface, with the specific architectural reasons they're unreachable (position:fixed pointer interception; the existing single-instance Tab-trap already blocking keyboard reach; zero interactive elements in any current MetricHelp/InfoBalloon content) unchanged since the first time they were raised. The two available fixes are also asymmetric in cost versus the problem: the Tab-trap fix is a narrow but fragile MUI-internals-coupled heuristic solving a problem that needs an unrelated future content change to manifest at all, while the aria-hidden/inert fix is a genuinely large undertaking (walking the DOM ancestor chain for a non-portaled overlay, state tracking/restoration, multi-instance coordination) for a path whose real-world reachability remains unverified against any actual screen reader after three review rounds with no access to one. Implementing either now would be adding real surface area and maintenance cost (more state to keep correct, more edge cases for future ChartFrame changes to accidentally break) against a documented non-issue, which is precisely the tradeoff this task's own dispatch explicitly authorized deciding against rather than forcing. If either scenario ever does become live -- a MetricHelp/InfoBalloon body gains an interactive element, or ChartFrame is ever used somewhere two instances can legitimately be open at once -- the concrete trigger itself (that content/usage change) is the right moment to revisit this, with a real defect to design and test the fix against rather than a hypothetical one.
decisions.alternatives_considered: Considered implementing the aria-hidden/inert half only (the 'small, well-contained change' the dispatch floated as a reasonable middle ground) by hiding ChartFrame's own immediate DOM siblings via a ref-based effect. Rejected: because the overlay isn't portaled to a fixed, shallow position (unlike a true Modal's root), ChartFrame's own immediate siblings at whatever depth it happens to be mounted at are usually just other elements within the same local layout (e.g. other cards in the same Grid row), not 'the rest of the page' -- a shallow one-level sibling hide would give a false sense of having fixed the gap while still leaving every ancestor level above that one fully reachable to assistive tech, which is worse than clearly documenting the gap as open.

comments.summary: No source code changes in this PR (2 task-board JSON files only). No API/schema changes (openapi.json n/a), no new module/dependency/layer (architecture-review n/a), no frontend component added or changed (placement-review n/a per step 7a -- nothing to assess), area is frontend/stocks not backend/signals|portfolio and skill is null, not verify-elder-signal (that check n/a). Decision memory: both closed checklist items have a corresponding decisions entry (task-worker, 2026-10-02T23:25:57Z) with decision + rationale + alternatives_considered, satisfying CLAUDE.md's decision-memory requirement -- no undecided-but-implemented judgment call here since both items are closed with an explicit no-change decision, not silently dropped.

Agree this is a genuinely reasonable 'no change needed' call, not a rubber-stamped carry-forward: both findings have now been independently re-confirmed as unreachable across three separate review passes (PR #373 round 2, PR #375, and this task), the reasoning for non-implementation is asymmetric-cost-vs-benefit and explicitly considered a middle-ground alternative (a shallow one-level aria-hidden) and rejected it with a concrete reason (would give a false sense of having fixed the gap while leaving higher DOM ancestors still reachable). Ran an independent code-review pass (medium effort) against the diff as well -- no findings.

review.notes: Accepted.
